descriptionChirho: Active healing performed by an agent (God, a person) in the Qal stem, encompassing all finite verb forms, infinitives, and the infinitive absolute with transitive meaning 'to heal, cure, restore to health.'
Substantive (nominalized) use of the Qal active participle as a professional or titular noun meaning 'physician, healer, doctor,' including divine epithets like 'your healer' (Exod 15:26).
Passive healing in the Nifal stem, indicating that the subject undergoes or receives healing — 'to be healed, to be cured, to recover' — of persons, wounds, or afflictions.

Intensive/factitive healing in the Piel stem, denoting thorough medical treatment or decisive curative action — 'to treat medically, to heal completely, to cure' — often used of prophets or physicians applying remedies.
Metaphorical extension of the Piel stem applied to non-bodily objects — 'to repair, to mend, to restore' — used of repairing walls, altars, or structures (cf. 2 Chr 24:12; 1 Kgs 18:30).
Passive of the repair/mend sense in the Nifal stem — 'to be repaired, to be restored' — said of structures or things rather than persons.
Reflexive healing in the Hitpael stem — 'to seek healing for oneself, to get oneself cured, to undergo treatment' — indicating the subject's initiative in obtaining medical care.
